entries.source: CR-5 §6.9 (COMMAND_ROBUSTNESS_SPEC) — LIVE-tier delegation-resolution smoke. Corrected July 7, 2026 by the Phase-4 live-API probe.
entries.notes: LIVE-ONLY: confirms the live LLM RESOLVES a delegation verb (mode=anthropic, success, marshal recovered) — the precondition for the aggressive arm to fire. It deliberately does NOT assert a specific action: the live model does NOT reliably apply the §6.2 table (July 7 probe: 'Ney/Davout/Soult, deal with Mack' ALL resolved to action=scout), which is exactly WHY CR-5 routing is DETERMINISTIC. The personality-differentiated BEHAVIOR (Ney aggressive -> a delegation-inferred PURSUE, keyed on the MARSHAL'S personality, NOT the LLM action) is asserted deterministically at the router/endpoint tier (TestAggressiveArmTagsInferredPursue) + the live probe. Under mock a delegation degrades to ASK (guardrail e). Run via `python -m backend.ai.parser_eval --live`.

LIVE-ONLY (see cr5-deleg-aggressive-ney-resolves-live): the live parse resolves; the cautious->scout split is the DETERMINISTIC router's doing (route_arm keyed on Davout's personality), not the parser action, so no specific action is pinned (fragile against the non-deterministic model). Davout is cautious on the 1805 roster.

LIVE-ONLY. A LITERAL marshal refuses to guess -> the router ALWAYS asks (route_arm returns 'ask' for a literal marshal regardless of the parser action), so the parser action is irrelevant here and is not pinned. The definitive literal->ASK behavior is asserted deterministically at the endpoint tier (test_command_robustness_cr5_personality_disambiguation.py::TestAskArmEndpoint::test_literal_delegation_asks_not_attacks). Soult was reassigned cautious->literal at the gate so the ASK arm is player-reachable.

entries.source: ES-7 second pass (§0.6.8) — revoke checked BEFORE grant in the mock chain (substring rule), word-boundary verbs revoke/withdraw/rescind/stop/end/terminate/cancel.
entries.notes: Withdrawing the rente reopens the shortfall machinery (grace, then erosion) — executor-tier behavior, tested in test_estate_second_pass.py.

entries.source: ES-7 second pass review fix — the retreat branch's 'withdraw' clause carries a _mentions_pension guard so this reaches the revoke branch instead of ordering Ney to RETREAT (the review's confirmed MED misroute).
entries.notes: Keyword-order pin: retreat is checked ~140 lines earlier in the mock chain; without the guard this utterance parsed to action=retreat at confidence 0.9 (bypassing the LLM fallback even in live mode).

entries.source: ES-7 second pass review fix — revoke-intent synonyms (stop/end/terminate/cancel, word-boundary) must revoke, never re-grant (the review's confirmed opposite-action misroute).
entries.notes: Word boundaries matter: \bend\b must not fire on 'extend'/'spend'.

entries.source: ES-7 second pass review fix — recruit's \braise\b clause carries a _mentions_pension guard; 'raise his pension' is the everyday top-up verb the help text itself invites.
entries.notes: Without the guard this recruited infantry (gold + admin AP spent). Grant re-sizes to the current gap (REPLACE semantics).

VS-3 land grant. The nation rides target via the vassal-family nation resolution; the province stays in raw text (executor extracts by known-region match). Checklist step 12 action-coverage row for grant_region_to_vassal.

The 'grant X to <nation>' form is gated on a KNOWN nation after 'to', so it never shadows grant_dotation ('grant Ney the duchy of Swabia' has no 'to <nation>') or change_autonomy ('grant Holland autonomy' carries 'autonomy').
COLD parse: bare cede keys the action even with no live nation list (target resolution then depends on world context; the executor answers with eligibility guidance).
